subject: Legend is hard to read if shape='.'

messages.author: 3e3abd3fe49f41c3
messages.subject: Legend is hard to read if shape='.'
parts:
I am plotting O(25000) points in each of 40 graphs on a single plot where each plot has four colors.  The single pixel '.' shape does a good job of representing the data density and looks good when printed, but it makes the legend hard to read because the color for each category is represented by only a single pixel.  Is there an easy way to keep the single pixel point representation in the graph but use a larger glyph in the legend?

As a example of the graph with synthetic data, 

library(ggplot2)
nplot=40
npoint = 25000
ncat = 4
cats = sample(1:ncat, npoint*nplot, replace=TRUE)
d=data.frame(x=rnorm(npoint*nplot)+2*cats, y=rnorm(npoint*nplot), cats=factor(cats), plotnum=1:nplot) 
ggplot(d)+ geom_point(aes(x,y,color=cats),shape='.') + facet_wrap(~plotnum,ncol=8)

Thank you,
John Jumper

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: Legend is hard to read if shape='.'
parts:
hi, you can change the shape of legend, e.g.:

ggplot(d[1:100, ])+ geom_point(aes(x,y,color=cats),shape='.') +
guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 1)))
